_comment: Edit here, rerun explore.py, compare the contact sheet. {subject} and {style} are spliced in mid-sentence, so keep them lower-case phrases with no full stop. {palette} is filled from the scheme named in each variant. Each variant names one of three styles (the directions under test); within a style, change one thing per variant so a run isolates its effect. Variants with an image use the author's own photographs in ref/, so anything derived from them is ours to ship.

styles.clear: late-1990s translucent coloured plastic product, like an iMac G3 or a see-through Game Boy Color: glossy candy-coloured shell you can see into, internal parts visible and tinted by the plastic, soft internal glow, clean studio lighting, crisp simple forms, Y2K consumer electronics, no text, no lettering, no logos, no numbers
styles.techno: 1990s techno graphic design in the manner of a Designers Republic record sleeve or a Japanese electronics catalogue: flat spot colours, hard-edged geometric vector shapes, thin technical rules, registration crosshairs, a precise sense of a diagram, bold and minimal, no gradients, no photorealism, no text, no lettering, no logos, no numbers
styles.chrome: Y2K futurism: liquid chrome and iridescent plastic, soft blobby rounded forms, glossy reflections of a pale sky, a small lens flare, a 2000-era 3D render made for a music player, no text, no lettering, no logos, no numbers

subject: a MiniDisc: a small nearly square plastic cartridge with rounded corners, with a round recordable disc and a dark centre hub visible through the shell, and a flat sliding shutter along one edge
negative: text, letters, numbers, logo, Sony, watermark, signature, floppy disk, 3.5 inch diskette, save icon, CD, DVD, compact disc case, cassette, hands, wood, table, clutter
